spec.mechanism_to_eliminate: First-match-wins promotion chain in apply_promotions (verdict.py:466-490) where only the WINNING path is observable. Verified overlap surface: _try_structural_pass (271-281) applies NO content_class filter so it shadows every other path when structural metrics are clean; _try_image_enrichment (240), _try_cat_b (302) and _try_small_doc (351) all admit flat_* documents. _try_cat_a/_try_cat_b/_try_cat_c are already mutually exclusive via content_class (289/302/329). Because nothing records which non-winning paths also matched, any threshold change silently re-partitions documents between paths and surfaces only as a corpus regression waves later. Compounding this, _try_cat_a (284-293) is the ONLY path of six lacking an effectively_garbled guard (the other five check it at 246/279/312/335/359), and several eligibility literals are hardcoded outside VerdictThresholds so they never appear in the config snapshot. RETIRED as stale: the claims that source_selection bypasses _clamp_pass wholesale (it is gated on _is_image_enrichment at 443) and that paths lack a shared content-volume floor (a global floor precedes all paths at 420-428). The six _try_* helpers are ALREADY side-effect-free; do not 'make them pure'.
spec.strategy: Phase 1, behavior-neutral except VG-1: (1) VG-1 add `not sig.effectively_garbled` to _try_cat_a, matching the other five paths (HR#5 safety hole). (2) VG-2/3/4 hoist hardcoded literals into PipelineConfig + VerdictThresholds. (3) VG-5 _try_structural_pass returns 'structural_pass' instead of ''. (4) VG-6 evaluate all six paths, collect matches, take the FIRST in the existing order as winner (behavior-identical by construction) and record the full match list on a new VerdictResult.promotion_paths_matched tuple field. (5) VG-7 de-duplicate the _try_image_enrichment call. (6) Add a partition characterization test pinning (promotion_paths_matched, winner, verdict) for a golden table of feature vectors. Phase 2 (always-evaluated floor phase before path selection) is DEFERRED — the characterization baseline must exist first. Do NOT implement the rev-1 PromotionSpec/PROMOTION_REGISTRY design: it preserves evaluation order via PromotionSpec.priority and fixes none of VG-1/VG-5/VG-6.

spec.mechanism_to_eliminate: Single shared detect_garble kernel consumed by 13 callers across 9+ subsystems with three compounding blind spots: (1) 3 call sites hardcode had_presentation_forms=False in their ScriptContext fallback (verdict.py _try_image_enrichment, images.py _attempt_tesseract_raster_recovery, indexer.py pre-garble probe), bypassing the NFKC presentation-forms compensation that detect_garble lines 566-577 provide internally — Arabic PDFs whose presentation-form codepoints were normalized away before reaching these callers go undetected; (2) _garble_check_nodes per-node loop at garble.py:676 uses node.get("text") which returns empty for table nodes whose content lives in headers/rows/row_records, making per-node garble detection blind to table-block content while the whole-tree concatenation fallback (already fixed via _node_text_parts) only fires when zero per-node garbles are found; (3) garble_prongs digit_ratio prong gated by garble_digit_floor=500 at garble.py:398 skips all text shorter than 500 chars, letting genuinely garbled short numeric-junk OCR noise pass unchecked; additionally garble_prongs:410 assigns _effective_script but never uses it, leaving a dead-code gap for the script-mismatch Latin mojibake detection that Chain 5 requires.
spec.strategy: type-safe contract — (1) replace all 3 remaining had_presentation_forms=False hardcodings with _infer_presentation_forms(text) calls to close the NFKC presentation-forms gap uniformly across all callers; (2) fix _garble_check_nodes per-node text extraction to use _node_text_parts(node) via deferred import (matching the existing pattern in _collect_all_node_text) so per-node garble detection sees table content; (3) add a secondary short-text numeric-junk check below garble_digit_floor with a stricter threshold (>0.90 digits AND >=50 chars) to close the numeric-junk blind spot without false-positiving on legitimate short numeric content; (4) wire _effective_script into the latin_gibberish prong so that when expected_script is Arabic but text is predominantly Latin, a lower nonsense threshold fires the script_mismatch_latin prong catching Latin tessdata mojibake

spec.zone_name: OCR Recovery Cascade and Kill-Switch Conflation
spec.mechanism_to_eliminate: Three independently-evolving OCR concerns (page-level garble/low-content escalation, per-picture crop OCR, image-dominant promotion) share conflated kill-switches and decision surfaces: (1) _recover_low_content_ocr gates on pipeline_config.ocr_escalation_garble instead of a dedicated flag, so disabling garble OCR silently disables low-content recovery; (2) _recover_picture_results returning [] when the per-picture kill-switch fires leaves literal <!-- image --> markers in tree output with no stripping step; (3) decide_ocr_strategy ordered if-chain where sequence IS specification means re-entry guard position is load-bearing but invisible to callers; (4) recovery eligibility predicates check only state.first_defect, so garble detection firing as secondary defect behind NODE_COUNT_LOW never triggers garble-specific recovery; (5) _recover_image_dominant_ocr checks image_dominant_ocr_escalation_enabled while sharing _execute_ocr_retry with garble/low-content paths, coupling their success/failure metrics; (6) standalone .jpg/.png pipeline bypasses the per-picture OCR gate entirely, creating a decision-surface gap where image documents route through a separate code path.
spec.strategy: Decouple the three kill-switches into independent config flags, add a marker-cleanup step when per-picture OCR is skipped, and extract recovery eligibility into a defect-set predicate (not first_defect only). Specifically: (A) add ocr_escalation_low_content config flag so low-content recovery is independently gatable; (B) add strip_unresolved_image_markers() cleanup in picture_plane.py called when _recover_picture_results returns empty; (C) widen recovery eligibility to check all active defects (state.active_defects set) not just first_defect; (D) delete decide_ocr_mode wrapper -- all callers should use decide_ocr_strategy directly for the sealed OcrDecision contract.

spec.zone_name: Converter Chain Fallback and AGPL Gating
spec.mechanism_to_eliminate: The converter chain failure-policy logic (indexer.py:664-671) treats structural failures as unconditional WALK-to-next, silently advancing to AGPL-licensed converters with only a logger.warning and zero metric increment — violating HR4 which requires AGPL activation to be a conscious operator decision. The BLOCK_AGPL policy only fires for transient failures (lines 665-666), while structural failures fall through to the else-WALK branch (line 670) which logs but proceeds (lines 725-736). Additionally, the remote Docling version check (_check_remote_docling_version, remote.py:30-56) is warn-only — it never blocks conversion even when pipeline_version is stale — and _remote_pdf_to_markdown (remote.py:70-121) never forwards expected_script to the external service payload (lines 96-100), causing remote-converted documents to skip script-aware garble detection at the converter level.
spec.strategy: Type-safe contract: (1) Add GATE_AGPL_STRUCTURAL value to ConverterFailurePolicy enum so structural-to-AGPL walks are a distinct, testable policy branch rather than falling through WALK. (2) In the policy decision logic, when not-transient AND next-is-AGPL, assign GATE_AGPL_STRUCTURAL. Its handler increments AGPL_FALLBACK_TOTAL(reason="structural_walk") and checks a new config flag agpl_structural_fallback_enabled (default True for backward compat); when False, block the walk like BLOCK_AGPL. (3) Upgrade _check_remote_docling_version to raise a new RemoteVersionSkewError when remote pipeline_version < local AND a new config flag remote_version_enforce is True (default False for backward compat), so operators can opt in to hard-blocking stale remotes. (4) Add expected_script parameter to _remote_pdf_to_markdown and include it in the JSON payload, closing the script-forwarding gap at the client side (server-side contract change is out of scope but the field is now sent).

issues.issue: The instruction for code_target #4 (remote.py:30-56) places `raise RemoteVersionSkewError(...)` INSIDE the existing `try:` block that is closed by a broad `except Exception as e:` clause (verified: the try spans the entire version-fetch/skew-check logic, and the pipeline_version-skew logger.error the spec anchors on sits inside that try, directly above the except). As specified, the raised RemoteVersionSkewError would be immediately caught by that same broad except, logged as 'Could not fetch remote /version... skew detection disabled', and swallowed — never propagating to any caller. This makes the entire point-3 deliverable (opt-in hard-blocking of stale remotes) a complete no-op even when remote_version_enforce=True, while claiming success. The spec must restructure the try/except (e.g., raise the new error outside the try, or add an explicit `except RemoteVersionSkewError: raise` re-raise before the generic except) — this is not addressed anywhere in the code_target or constraint text.

issues.issue: Wiring check for RemoteVersionSkewError uses check_type 'isinstance' and lists remote.py under must_be_imported_by, but per the code target the class is DEFINED in remote.py (not imported there) and is only ever raised, never isinstance()-checked or caught anywhere in the spec (no except RemoteVersionSkewError block is added by any code_target). issues.issue: The mechanism_to_eliminate frames AGPL structural fallback as entirely uncontrolled, but the codebase already has a pervasive `allow_agpl_fallback`/ALLOW_AGPL_FALLBACK flag (config.py, used in indexer.py, pipeline.py, docling_conv.py, formats.py, pictures.py) that — when False — excludes the AGPL pymupdf4llm converter from the chain entirely, making the described structural-walk-to-AGPL scenario impossible in that mode. The spec's new agpl_structural_fallback_enabled flag is a finer-grained control for when allow_agpl_fallback=True, which is legitimate (analogous to the existing BLOCK_AGPL vs allow_agpl_fallback split) but the spec never acknowledges the existing flag as prior art, risking two similarly-named, easily-confused AGPL config toggles for operators.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a note in the spec's how/constraint text distinguishing agpl_structural_fallback_enabled from the existing allow_agpl_fallback, and/or name it more distinctly (e.g. block_agpl_structural_walk) to reduce operator confusion.

spec.zone_name: Dual-Writer Verdict Persistence and Consistency Model Split
spec.mechanism_to_eliminate: Three independent verdict writers (_upsert_registry_row, _drain_verdict_retry_queue, save_doc_meta from child) share no unified consistency contract. The catch-all exception handler in _upsert_registry_row (line 156) silently drops verdict_fields on Postgres upsert failure -- retry is only enqueued on pool-not-ready (line 105), not on transient query/network errors, permanently losing verdict data. The registry DELETE SQL (queries.py:244) lacks a server-side statement_timeout, meaning asyncpg's client-side timeout kills the coroutine but leaves the Postgres query running. When registry_enabled=false at runtime, the consistency model silently degrades from Postgres-authoritative to sidecar-only with eventual consistency, with no metric, no sidecar stamp, and no alert surface for operators.
spec.strategy: consolidate -- (1) Enqueue verdict retry on ALL Postgres failures in _upsert_registry_row, not just pool-not-ready, closing the silent verdict loss gap. (2) Add SQL-level statement_timeout to DELETE via a transaction block so Postgres kills the query server-side. (3) Add a REGISTRY_CONSISTENCY_DEGRADED Prometheus gauge (bridged via Redis like existing registry metrics) incremented when the sidecar-only fallback path fires, giving operators an alert surface. (4) Stamp consistency_regime in the sidecar during _upsert_registry_row backfill so the runtime regime is forensically visible in stored metadata.

issues.issue: Sub-strategy #4 (stamp consistency_regime in the sidecar) is non-functional as specified. save_doc_meta (src/pageindex_mcp/storage/verdict.py:78-197) is NOT a generic dict merge -- it copies fields into the output sidecar only via three hardcoded whitelists: _base_fields (line 39-42 area), _MERGE_FIELDS (lines 142-164), and _FACET_FIELDS (line 35). Verified by reading the full function body: any key not in these three tuples, whether present in the incoming `meta` dict or in the previously-stored `existing` sidecar, is silently dropped on every write -- confirmed 'consistency_regime' appears in none of them (grep across src/pageindex_mcp/ shows zero prior occurrences of the string; only the pre-existing, differently-named 'consistency_model' field is unconditionally hardcoded at line 181). So both proposed calls -- winning['consistency_regime']='postgres-authoritative' before save_doc_meta(doc_id, winning), and save_doc_meta(doc_id, {'consistency_regime': 'sidecar-only'}) -- will write a sidecar with NO consistency_regime key at all. The spec lists storage/verdict.py in key_files but has zero code_targets touching it to extend _MERGE_FIELDS, and zero wiring_checks covering this. Consequently test_requirement #6 (tests/test_storage.py, 'save_doc_meta preserves existing consistency_regime field ... assert consistency_regime is preserved') will FAIL against the real implementation -- the field is stripped on the read-merge-write round trip, not preserved. Test requirements #3 and #4 in tests/test_registry.py only mock save_doc_meta and inspect the call arguments, so they would pass while masking this exact production bug.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a code_target for src/pageindex_mcp/storage/verdict.py adding 'consistency_regime' to _MERGE_FIELDS (or a dedicated whitelist), and add a corresponding wiring_check / non-mocked integration test that round-trips save_doc_meta and reads back the actual persisted JSON to confirm consistency_regime survives -- not just that it was passed into a mocked call.

issues.issue: The constraint on the new Gauge ('Must be a Gauge (not Counter) because it is bridged via Redis SET/INCRBY like the other registry metrics') mischaracterizes the actual bridge mechanism the spec chose. The spec directs use of the newer, generic _BRIDGED_METRICS / _mirror_bridged_incr path (metrics/sync.py), whose own docstring states the mechanism works via each metric's internal `_value` attribute 'shared by Counter/Gauge/Histogram-without-buckets ... without needing every bridged metric to be a Gauge.' The Gauge-must-be-used reasoning actually applies only to the older, separate REGISTRY_WRITE_FAILURES_TOTAL/_sync_registry_metrics_from_redis pattern the spec does NOT use here. Harmless (Gauge still works fine), but the stated rationale is factually wrong.
